l1a4.label: Activity
l1a4.title: Do or Background?
l1a4.intro: Grace sent this chat. For each sentence, choose Do if it asks you to do something (including "don't" and "only"), or Background if it only gives news, a reason, or a greeting.

items.q: "Hi Ana, quick one before the weekend."
items.good: A greeting. Nothing to do yet.
items.try: This is only a greeting. Nothing is asked.

items.q: "Our holiday orders doubled last year, so we're preparing earlier this time."
items.good: It explains why, but doesn't ask for anything.
items.try: It sounds urgent, but it only explains why Grace is preparing early. No task is in this sentence.

items.q: "Could you make a copy of last year's Holiday Orders sheet and name it Holiday Orders 2026?"
items.good: A request, even though it's written as a question.
items.try: "Could you…?" is a polite way to ask for work. This is the main task.

items.q: "Last year the sheet got confusing because people typed dates in different ways."
items.good: It's the reason for the next sentence.
items.try: This describes a past problem. The instruction about it comes in the next sentence.

items.q: "So in the new one, please use one date format only: YYYY-MM-DD."
items.good: "Please use one date format only" is an instruction, and a limit.
items.try: It follows a reason, but "please use… only" asks you to do something. It's a limit for your Task Card.

items.q: "Joy might ask you about it; she's new and still learning our system."
items.good: Useful to know, but nothing is asked of you.
items.try: It sounds like you might need to act, but Grace doesn't ask for anything here.

items.q: "Don't delete anything from last year's sheet; we still need it for taxes."
items.good: "Don't delete anything" is a limit. The tax part is the reason.
items.try: "Don't delete anything" is something you must follow, so it counts as Do. The reason is attached, but the limit is the instruction.

items.q: "Thanks so much, you've been a big help this month!"
items.good: A kind closing. Nothing to do.
items.try: This is a thank-you. Nothing is asked.

l1a5b.label: Activity
l1a5b.title: Convert the Deadline

feedback: That's Grace's time, not yours. Add 15 hours: Friday 1 AM in the Philippines.
That subtracts the 15 hours. Portland is behind the Philippines, so you add: Friday 1 AM.
Thursday 10 AM + 15 hours = Friday 1 AM. Plan to finish Thursday evening your time.
The day moves forward, and the hour changes too: 10 AM + 15 hours = 1 AM Friday.

options: Late Wednesday night to early Thursday, Philippine time
feedback: When Grace writes, it's 6 AM Tuesday in Portland, so her "tomorrow morning" is Wednesday morning there. 9 AM Wednesday in Portland is 12 AM Thursday for you.
That's your tomorrow. Grace means her tomorrow: Wednesday morning in Portland, which is around midnight Wednesday night for you.
It's 6 AM Tuesday for Grace when she writes, so "tomorrow" is Wednesday there. You have until about midnight Wednesday night your time.
That's a few hours too late. Wednesday morning in Portland is late Wednesday night to early Thursday for you.

About Saturday 8 AM Philippine time (5 PM Friday hers), and add "exact EOD time?" to Open questions
Friday 5 PM, Philippine time, since that's a normal end of workday
Any time on Friday, since no hour was given, so there's nothing to note
feedback: EOD usually means the end of the client's workday, not yours. If it's 5 PM Friday in Portland, that's Saturday 8 AM for you. And because "EOD" isn't an exact time, note it as an open question.
EOD usually means around 5 PM her time, which is Saturday 8 AM for you. Since she didn't say an exact time, you also note it as an open question.
That's the end of your workday, not Grace's. Her 5 PM Friday is Saturday 8 AM for you, and the exact time should go under Open questions.
A missing hour is something to note, not ignore. Write down your best reading (about Saturday 8 AM your time) and add the exact time to Open questions.

Monday end of day, Philippine time
No deadline, because Grace didn't give an exact time
